items.title: Overview
items.text: This breakout board is a high-performance hardware hub for the pyControl project. Driven by the cross-platform open-source GUI software, it is able to interface with a variety of peripheral devices to record inputs and control outputs for behavioral experiments.

items.title: Performance
items.text:
The goal is to keep latency below the 1ms timestamp resolution of the pyControl framework. The high load setup is an extreme condition, where the M4 processor on the pyControl Breakout 1.2 began showing some limitations. The H7 Breakout 0.9 performs great in all conditions.

The benchmarking method is described in the pyControl manuscript (see "Framework Performance" in the results section and "Framework performance validation" in the materials and methods section).

Flash availability

There is a memory shortage right now, so availability can be suspect. This PCB design includes both 8-WSON (8x6) and 8-SOIC footprints to accommodate multiple packages of Winbond Quad SPI Flash Memory operating at 3.3V. Here is a Digi-Key search for parts that match the requirements

items.title: Startup Modes
items.text:
Press the top User button (Button A) and then press the Reset button. The LEDs will cycle through the following modes below. Release the user button to enter the mode.

LED Color Mode What it does 🔴 Red Factory reset Reformats the /flash filesystem on the QSPI chip as FAT and adds fresh boot.py, main.py, README.txt and pybcdc.inf. Everything on the flash is erased, including the pyControl framework and task files. 🟡 Yellow Safe mode Skips boot.py and main.py. The filesystem still mounts and you get a REPL. It only applies to that one boot; the next reset, even a soft reset (Ctrl-D), boots normally. 🟢 Green Normal Runs boot.py then main.py, the same as a plain reset.
